data.content_ref: inline:SRC_002 claims the expert dominates on configural tasks and the panel on linear tasks, making a task x estimator interaction the distinguishing evidence. But when the checklist itself encodes interaction terms (SRC_002's own third countercondition: decision trees with branching), the panel need not be configural-weak: it can handle configural outcomes by branching, collapsing the predicted interaction. In that realistic regime there is no task type on which the expert is predicted to dominate, so the interaction diagnostic becomes unobservable by construction and cannot serve as the single distinguishing evidence the problem demands. SRC_002 offers no fallback evidence for the common case where a well-designed checklist captures interactions.
